notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null); no hardware was attached and no hardware run is claimed.

WHAT IT SERVES: the card's models[0], src/mjlab_manipulation/robots/droid/xmls/droid.xml, as a MujocoDriver in simulated mode R0. cap.world.step.v1 takes {ticks, action: {ctrl: [...]}}; each ctrl element is checked by the bridge against the model's actuator_ctrlrange before data.ctrl is written, then mj_step runs ticks times. The seven position actuators use the arm default class's inheritrange=1, so their control ranges follow the seven joint ranges (droid.xml:13-15, :96-143, :160-167). cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults with mj_resetData + mj_forward. The state is the bridge's integration state (time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms, seed). The card's other models (gen3.xml, kuka.xml, ur5e.xml, xarm/hand.xml, and the xarm.xml and Robotiq 2f85 files named in the hints) are other devices and are not served; per PLAYBOOK section 8 a MujocoDriver loads models[0].

WHY THIS SHAPE: the card is family-config with helper MujocoDriver and the upstream provides MJCF assets, not a Python device class. MuJoCo is not installed and cannot be installed where the gate runs (no network, no pip), so backends['fake'] is this package's stand-in mujoco module in fake.py, declared as the callable fake_mujoco. The stand-in parses the same MJCF text for the joint dimensions, the actuator control ranges and the option time step, but integrates a placeholder motion of each actuated joint; it loads no mesh and resolves no contact, equality, tendon or actuator constraint. The fidelity gaps list every difference, and MuJoCo itself was never imported, so no trajectory was compared with the real engine. The sim backend (the real mujoco module) was not run.

RISK/STOP: simulated R0; cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1 are both catalogue R0 classes, there is no hardware backend and no physical effect, so no hardware independent stop is claimed; the e-stop is the runtime's software latch, as for the simulator families. No operator-required limit is needed because the control envelope is the model's own.

LIMITS: the package declares no Limit of its own. The bridge derives action.ctrl from the model's actuator_ctrlrange at run time (source upstream_code, reference the model file); the runtime refuses an out-of-range element before writing data.ctrl.

LICENSE: the clone has no repository-level LICENSE file; only the vendored Robotiq 2f85 directory carries one. The card and the lock pin license_spdx NOASSERTION and license_class unknown; a maintainer should confirm the license before publication.

WARNINGS (all expected, none failed): G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND because the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco module rather than a package class the gate can wrap in a Recorder; G8.NO_UNIT x3 for seed, ticks and action.ctrl[*], the integer/numeric inputs the simulator family derives (PLAYBOOK.md section 8). No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised; every Fact cites a README, pyproject.toml, droid.xml or constants line of the clone.

TESTS: test_driver.py keeps mhs.testing.check_driver and adds seven cases (model shape, control envelope, step effect, reset, fidelity contract, e-stop latch, card model file); they pass. No catalogue_requests: the package uses only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1.
